name: Verify
grades: A: no errors and at most 1 warning. B: no errors. C: 1 error. D: 2 errors. F: 3 or more. Each rule counts once, however many places it fires. Hints never count.

1.name: Title that says what to do

2.name: Back, close or cancel at the top

3.name: Says where the code or link was sent

5.name: Button to send the code or move on

v1.name: Separate code boxes
expect: A title that says what to do, near the top
One box or slot per digit, with no submit button
A back or close control at the top
The number keypad open under the form

v2.name: One field, one button
v2.lead: Code in one field with a button
expect: A title that says what to do, near the top
A line saying where the code was sent
A single code field with a button to send it
A back or close control at the top

v4.name: Identity check without a sent code
v4.lead: Identity check without a sent code

not_checked: What happens after the last digit or the tap on the button: whether the code sends itself, and what a wrong code shows.
The countdown on the resend control: one screenshot holds a single moment of it.

rules.says: Text or a close control is too faint against what is behind it.
rules.why: Accessibility guidelines ask for 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text: 18 pt, or 14 pt bold (button labels are bold). Controls, such as a close or back glyph, need 3:1. Below 3:1 is an error; from 3:1 to 4.5:1 on smaller text it is a warning. Checked on the labels of buttons, the lines of the parts marked as key text, and the close and back glyphs. Not checked on a dimmed screen or over a photo or a pattern.

rules.says: Text is smaller than 11 pt.
rules.why: Apple lists 11 pt as the smallest text size on iOS. Measured from the height of each line, so it is about right, not exact. Checked on the parts marked as key text.

rules.says: A control sits under the status bar or the home indicator.
rules.why: The status bar row at the top and the bottom 34 pt, where the home indicator sits, belong to the system on phones without a home button. Flagged when a control reaches the status bar row or comes within 17 pt of the bottom edge, so a button that only touches the area is not counted.

rules.says: A close or back control is drawn smaller than 13 pt.
rules.why: Apple asks for a 44 x 44 pt tap area. The standard close X in a bar is drawn about 13 to 17 pt across inside that area, so only a smaller drawing is flagged. A screenshot cannot show the tap area itself, so this is a hint.
